newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Hariri to resign October 15 - sources.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Hariri to resign October 15 - sources.

text.p: Lebanon's Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and his government will resign on October 15 to make way for the formation of a new government following recent parliamentary elections, government sources said on Thursday.
"On October 15 the Hariri government will resign and afterwards President Elias Hrawi will consult with the parliamentary deputies to decide on their choice of a new prime minister," a source said.
Hariri, who has been prime minister since October 1992, is expected to be reappointed and form a new government -- his third in four years -- after parliament holds its first meeting on October 22.

The 51-year-old billionaire construction tycoon won a seat representing Beirut at his first attempt in the elections last month and will head a group of about 20 supporters -- one of the biggest blocs in the 128-member parliament.

The sources said it was likely that Hariri would not be re-appointed until after a visit to Lebanon by French President Jacques Chirac, which is expected on October 24-25, and the government would stay on in a caretaker capacity until then.

Parliament is due to elect a Speaker at its first meeting on October 22, and Hrawi's consultations with the deputies on the choice of a new prime minister are expected to start immediately after this.
Hrawi is bound under the constitution to accept the majority decision of the deputies in choosing a new prime minister. However, consultations will probably be interrupted by Chirac's visit.
The sources said it was likely that the appointment of the new prime minister and government -- which must receive a vote of approval from parliament -- would be completed by the end of October.
